payload.summary: PLAN_REVIEW round 3 reaches the configured maximum without convergence. The revision closes the prior package ownership, inventory, timeout/evidence, distributed-budget, and egress-topology blockers, and both strict OpenSpec and work-package validation pass. Four critical blockers remain: the process-health DDL references undeclared lifecycle columns; nullable SQL equality still lets duplicated queue correlation disappear; generated Python/cursor bounds drift from the canonical signed-BIGINT contracts; and the context contracts admit malformed or internally inconsistent W3C carriers. One non-blocking SQL bound nit also remains. External multi-vendor dispatch remains policy-blocked, so the safe consensus is single-reviewer and lacks cross-vendor quorum.
completed_work: Re-read the third revision's contracts, design, specs, tasks, and work-package changes against the round-2 findings.

Confirmed that prior operator-credential ownership, complete entrypoint inventory, package write scopes, integration union, soak timeout/evidence, local attempt budget, and concrete Squid policy findings are closed.
Reproduced that the generated Pydantic page and ownership models accept 9999999999999999999 in fields whose OpenAPI contract is bounded to signed BIGINT.
Identified executable DDL failure from lifecycle_kind/expires_at references without column declarations and the PostgreSQL CHECK UNKNOWN bypass for nullable duplicated correlation columns.
Identified missing W3C carrier syntax and cross-field validation across JSON Schema, OpenAPI, and generated Python contracts.
Validated review-findings-plan.json against openspec/schemas/review-findings.schema.json, ran strict OpenSpec validation, and ran the work-package schema/DAG/lock validator successfully.
Did not retry the prohibited external vendor dispatch; regenerated a safe single-reviewer consensus and recorded the policy constraint.

decisions.title: Outcome is max_iter
decisions.rationale: This is the third configured PLAN_REVIEW pass and four directly evidenced contract blockers remain, so implementation cannot safely begin and the review loop has exhausted max_phase_iterations.

decisions.title: SQL equality must be null-safe
decisions.rationale: PostgreSQL CHECK constraints accept UNKNOWN; nullable '=' comparisons therefore do not establish the plan's claimed equality invariant when canonical context exists.

decisions.title: Trace Context validation is an ingress security contract
decisions.rationale: Length-only validation permits malformed or split trace identity to cross service boundaries and contaminate audit correlation, contrary to the explicit W3C and untrusted-input requirements.

next_steps: Escalate after max iteration: add lifecycle_kind/expires_at columns and class-specific expiry enforcement, then parse and migration-test the DDL.
Replace nullable queue duplicate comparisons with presence requirements plus IS NOT DISTINCT FROM and test every null/mismatch case.
Regenerate all bounded Python fields, use ClaimGenerationString for attempt cursors, and enforce max/max+1 drift tests across every contract surface.
Add generated W3C traceparent/tracestate syntax and semantic cross-field validation with malformed and trace-mismatch ingress tests.
External vendor quorum still requires explicit permission to share repository-derived plan details with configured vendor services.
